editorial:
Imagine you are a writer who gets way too involved in a crime story. That is exactly what happens to Jenny, a columnist who cannot stop thinking about a weird murder at her sister's school. You get to follow her as she sneaks onto campus to play detective, hoping to catch a killer before more people get hurt. The movie has a strange mix of moods, jumping from funny moments to creepy scenes where people start dying one by one. It feels like a deadly game of hide-and-seek where the killer is treating the murders like some kind of dark art project.

You will probably love how the mystery builds up, even if the pacing feels a bit uneven at times. The acting is solid and keeps you guessing about who is actually behind the killings. While some of the scares are a bit dated, the twists are still fun to watch. It is a great pick if you enjoy weird thrillers that do not take themselves too seriously.
endingExplained: The big twist reveals that the killer was using the deaths to create a piece of art. Jenny eventually finds out that the person she trusted was actually the one orchestrating the whole thing. In the final scenes, the killer tries to make Jenny the final part of the masterpiece. After a tense struggle, the truth comes out and the cycle of violence finally ends, though the ending leaves you feeling a bit unsettled.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves quirky mysteries with a dark twist.
